title: Multiclot in Anticoagulation Diagnostics: Correlation of Direct Oral Anticoagulants with Viscoelastic Coagulation Parameters in the RVV and ECA Tests
summary:
Many people take blood-thinning tablets to protect themselves against strokes or blood clots. These medications are called "direct oral anticoagulants". When such patients need heart surgery, it is very important for the treatment team to know whether these medications are still active or have already been broken down by the body. A residual effect that is too strong can lead to bleeding during or after surgery.
Usually, this residual effect is measured in the laboratory. However, these tests take time, which can be problematic in emergencies or shortly before surgery. In the operating room, rapid clotting tests are therefore used in addition, providing results within minutes. There are special tests that can specifically detect the effect of these blood-thinning medications.
At University Hospital Bonn, a new device for these rapid tests is being used in routine care. It replaces a previously used device that is no longer reliably available in the long term. 
This study aims to examine how closely the results of the rapid tests on the new device match the laboratory-measured drug levels of the blood-thinning medications. The study uses only data that arise during normal medical care. No additional examinations, no additional blood draws, and no changes in treatment will be performed. Approximately 65 patients will be evaluated over a period of twelve months.
conditions: Perioperative coagulation management in cardiac surgery patients on treatment with direct oral anticoagulants, including assessment of residual anticoagulant effects of factor Xa inhibitors (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban) and direct thrombin inhibitors (dabigatran) in the context of cardiopulmonary bypass.

Adult cardiac surgery patients (≥18 years) with intake of direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) receiving routine clinical care at University Hospital Bonn.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years, Performance of cardiac surgery, performance of viscoelastic and coagulation testing as part of routine clinical practice,  use of DOACs
Exclusion criteria:
No Multiclot or coagulation testing performed
